2. STEP 1 — INDEPENDENT DESIGN CLASSIFICATION & TOOL SELECTION (`RISK_OF_BIAS.md` §1):
   Classify the study's actual design from its Methods section, then select the matching appraisal tool:
   - `"RoB 2 (parallel-trial variant)"`: Individually randomized controlled trial. Rate all 5 domains (`D1` Randomization process; `D2` Deviations from intended interventions; `D3` Missing outcome data; `D4` Measurement of the outcome; `D5` Selection of the reported result) as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`, and overall rating as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`.
   - `"RoB 2 (cluster-randomized trials variant)"`: Cluster-randomized trial (villages, compounds, neighbourhoods, schools, utilities randomized as clusters). Rate all 6 domains (`D1a` Randomization process; `D1b` Timing of identification or recruitment of participants within clusters; `D2` Deviations from intended interventions; `D3` Missing outcome data; `D4` Measurement of the outcome; `D5` Selection of the reported result) as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`, and overall rating as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`.
   - `"ROBINS-I"`: Non-randomized study of an intervention / policy with a genuine comparator (DiD, IV, RDD, PSM, ITS, controlled before-after, comparative longitudinal/panel evaluation). Rate all 7 domains (`D1` Bias due to confounding; `D2` Bias in selection of participants into the study; `D3` Bias in classification of interventions; `D4` Bias due to deviations from intended interventions; `D5` Bias due to missing data; `D6` Bias in measurement of outcomes; `D7` Bias in selection of the reported result — note `No information` honestly if no pre-analysis plan/protocol exists) as `"Low"`, `"Moderate"`, `"Serious"`, `"Critical"`, or `"No information"`, and overall rating in the same vocabulary. Do NOT assign single-case histories with no comparator arm to ROBINS-I!
   - `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies"`: Quantitative cross-sectional survey / observational regression without a quasi-experimental intervention structure. Rate all 8 items (`Q1` Inclusion criteria in sample clearly defined; `Q2` Study subjects and setting described in detail; `Q3` Exposure measured validly and reliably; `Q4` Objective, standard criteria used for measurement of condition; `Q5` Confounding factors identified; `Q6` Strategies to deal with confounding factors stated; `Q7` Outcomes measured validly and reliably; `Q8` Appropriate statistical analysis used) as `"Yes"`, `"No"`, `"Unclear"`, or `"Not applicable"`. Provide overall narrative judgment (`"Low concern"`, `"Some concern"`, or `"High concern"` — no numeric score).
   - `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies"`: Observational comparative cohort design (not framed as a ROBINS-I intervention). Rate all 11 items (`Q1` Similar groups from same population; `Q2` Exposures measured similarly; `Q3` Exposure measured validly/reliably; `Q4` Confounding factors identified; `Q5` Strategies to deal with confounding stated; `Q6` Participants free of outcome at start; `Q7` Outcomes measured validly/reliably; `Q8` Follow-up time reported and sufficient; `Q9` Follow-up complete or loss explored; `Q10` Strategies to address incomplete follow-up utilized; `Q11` Appropriate statistical analysis used) as `"Yes"`, `"No"`, `"Unclear"`, or `"Not applicable"`, plus narrative overall judgment (`"Low concern"`, `"Some concern"`, `"High concern"`).
   - `"CASP Qualitative Checklist"`: Primary qualitative study (interviews, ethnography, focus groups, qualitative documentary/field case study). Rate all 10 items (`Q1` Clear statement of aims; `Q2` Qualitative methodology appropriate; `Q3` Research design appropriate to address aims; `Q4` Recruitment strategy appropriate to aims; `Q5` Data collected in a way that addressed research issue; `Q6` Relationship between researcher and participants adequately considered [reflexivity]; `Q7` Ethical issues considered; `Q8` Data analysis sufficiently rigorous; `Q9` Clear statement of findings; `Q10` How valuable is the research [narrative assessment]). Rate Q1-Q9 `"Yes"`, `"No"`, or `"Can't tell"`, and Q10 narratively; give narrative `overall_rating` (e.g. `"Low methodological concern"`, `"Moderate concern (X Can't tell / No items)"`, `"High methodological concern"` — no numeric score).
   - `"MMAT (Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool)"`: Genuine mixed-methods primary study combining qualitative AND quantitative empirical components (do NOT assign purely quantitative or purely qualitative studies to MMAT). Rate Screening `S1`-`S2`, Qualitative `1.1`-`1.5`, the matching Quantitative 5-item block (`2.1`-`2.5` randomized, `3.1`-`3.5` non-randomized, or `4.1`-`4.5` descriptive), AND Mixed-Methods integration `5.1`-`5.5` (`5.1` adequate rationale for mixed methods; `5.2` components effectively integrated; `5.3` outputs of integration adequately interpreted; `5.4` divergences/inconsistencies adequately addressed; `5.5` components adhere to quality criteria of each tradition) as `"Yes"`, `"No"`, or `"Can't tell"`. Per MMAT 2018 rules, NEVER compute a numeric score; provide a concise criterion-grounded narrative `overall_rating` noting that overall quality cannot exceed the weakest component.
   - `"AMSTAR 2"`: Secondary systematic review, meta-analysis, or scoping review with an explicit systematic search/screening method (NEVER apply AMSTAR 2 to non-systematic narrative literature reviews!). Rate all 16 items `Q1`-`Q16` (explicitly marking critical domains `Q2`, `Q4`, `Q7`, `Q9`, `Q11`, `Q13`, `Q15`) as `"Yes"`, `"Partial Yes"` (where applicable), `"No"`, or `"Not applicable (no meta-analysis)"`, and apply AMSTAR 2 overall confidence (`"High"`, `"Moderate"`, `"Low"`, `"Critically Low"`).
   - `"Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework"`: Doctrinal-empirical hybrid, jurimetric analysis, or institutional/legal-historical case study that fits NONE of the six conventional designs above. Rate all 13 narrative domains (`D1` Legal source accuracy; `D2` Jurisdictional specificity; `D3` Exposure definition; `D4` Outcome definition; `D5` Sampling transparency; `D6` Selection process; `D7` Measurement transparency; `D8` Causal identification; `D9` Treatment of confounding; `D10` Institutional context; `D11` Replication potential; `D12` Coding transparency; `D13` Researcher reflexivity) as `"strong"`, `"adequate"`, `"weak"`, or `"not assessable"`. Explicitly frame `overall_rating` as a structured non-validated judgment (NEVER a numeric composite score!).
   - `"NONE"`: Use when the study fits NONE of the listed instruments (e.g., pure mathematical/simulation optimization model with no empirical sample, or non-systematic narrative essay/review with no primary empirical method and no systematic search). Set `overall_rating = "NOT APPLICABLE (design fits no listed tool)"`, explain clearly in `why_tool_chosen` and `overall_narrative_summary` rather than forcing an inappropriate checklist, and still fill the 7 `cross_tool_domains` honestly from the paper!

cross_tool_domains.attrition: Moderate-to-high administrative missingness/non-response: of the 20 BHL-headquartered municipalities, 13 (65%) lacked complete 2016-2017 SNIS sewage data; after primary LAI/e-SIC requests, 4 municipalities failed to respond, 1 reported having collection without recorded data, and 3 supplied only partial or single-year data, reducing analytic denominators to 12-17 municipalities across service and investment indicators.
cross_tool_domains.confounding: High risk / unaddressed for causal claims: the study uses unadjusted descriptive comparisons across municipalities and between 2016 and 2017 without accounting for municipal fiscal capacity, GDP, population size, service provider model (state utility vs. direct municipal provision), or physical geography.
cross_tool_domains.legal_measurement_quality: Strong doctrinal grounding and adequate empirical operationalization: accurately analyzes CF/88, Lei 11.445/2007, Decreto 7.217/2010, deadline-extension decrees through Decreto 9.254/2017, STJ tariff precedent (with one minor text slip writing STF on PDF p. 20), and Lei 12.527/2011 (LAI), and directly operationalizes municipal compliance via IBGE MUNIC 2017 PMSB status and primary e-SIC/physical LAI audit filings.
cross_tool_domains.measurement_bias: Moderate concern: relies on standardized SNIS codes (IN015, IN056, FN024, FN043, FN053), BCB IGP-DI deflation, and IBGE MUNIC 2017, plus direct observation of e-SIC portal functionality, but depends on unaudited municipal/utility self-reporting (including contradictory initial vs. subsequent responses in Almadina) and omits municipality labels on the horizontal axes of Figures 1 and 2.
cross_tool_domains.outcome_measurement_quality: Adequate for descriptive benchmarking: uses standard SNIS sewage collection (IN015), treatment (IN056), and population coverage indicators for 2016-2017 alongside QGIS watershed mapping, but suffers from missing municipal data in 3-8 municipalities per indicator, unlabelled bars in Figures 1-2, and a discrepancy between the text ('13 municípios') and the 12 municipalities listed in Table 1.
cross_tool_domains.reporting_bias: Moderate concern: no pre-analysis plan or protocol; governance and LAI outcomes are transparently tabulated for all 20 municipalities (Table 2, Quadro 1, Table 3), but Figures 1 and 2 omit x-axis municipality labels in the published PDF and Table 1 displays 12 municipal rows despite the text citing 13 analyzed municipalities.
cross_tool_domains.selection_bias: Low at the design stage (census of all 20 municipalities with urban headquarters inside the Bacias Hidrográficas do Leste), but moderate-to-high selection bias from non-reporting in quantitative service and investment analyses because municipalities without SNIS records or LAI responses are omitted from indicator averages.

domain_ratings.justification: Accurately cites and interprets primary Brazilian constitutional, statutory, regulatory, and judicial authorities—including CF/88 arts. 5º XXXIII and 175-176, Lei 11.445/2007, Decreto 7.217/2010 and subsequent deadline-extension decrees (8.211/2014, 8.629/2015, 9.254/2017), Lei 12.527/2011 (LAI), Lei 8.987/1995, Lei 7.783/1989, UN Resolution A/RES/64/292, and STJ precedent (AgRg no REsp 1505229/PR)—with only a minor typographical slip referring to STF instead of STJ on PDF p. 20.

Clearly specifies both the vertical allocation of constitutional competence (municipal titularity over local basic sanitation services) and the exact geographic and temporal scope: the 20 municipalities whose urban headquarters lie within the Bacias Hidrográficas do Leste (BHL / RPGA-Leste) in Bahia, Brazil, evaluated for 2016-2017 (with primary LAI requests conducted in 2019).

Clearly defines the legal-institutional governance obligations and fiscal inputs assessed—existence or drafting stage of the Plano Municipal de Saneamento Básico (PMSB) in IBGE MUNIC 2017, municipal e-SIC portal availability and statutory 20+10 day response compliance under Lei 12.527/2011, and deflated per capita sewage investment ((FN024+FN043+FN053)/POP)—though these are examined descriptively alongside outcomes rather than modeled as an explanatory exposure.

domain_ratings.justification: Defines sanitation universalization outcomes using standardized national SNIS indicators—sewage collection rate (IN015), treated sewage relative to water consumed (IN056), and municipal population attendance rate—supplemented by administrative LAI response categories.

Explicitly states the geographic sampling frame: out of 24 municipalities intersecting the 9,507 km² BHL region, all 20 municipalities with urban headquarters ('sedes municipais') inside the watershed (total population 635,546 in 2017) are named and included.

Includes the full census of 20 BHL-headquartered municipalities for PMSB and LAI governance tables, avoiding sampling discretion, but indicator-level subsamples drop to 12, 13, or 17 municipalities due to missing SNIS and LAI data, with a discrepancy between 13 stated and 12 listed municipalities in Table 1 and missing x-axis municipality labels in Figures 1 and 2.

domain_ratings.justification: Identifies exact administrative indicator codes (SNIS IN015, IN056, FN024, FN043, FN053), IGP-DI inflation adjustment to December 2017 prices via the Banco Central calculator, IBGE MUNIC 2017, SEI population estimates, and QGIS Noosa 3.6.3, but is weakened by omitted x-axis labels in Figures 1 and 2 and reliance on unverified municipal self-reports.

domain_ratings.justification: Purely descriptive cross-sectional and two-year (2016-2017) tabular/graphical comparison without any counterfactual, quasi-experimental design, or statistical test to identify the causal effect of PMSB adoption, LAI governance, or investment on sewage coverage or treatment.

No empirical measurement or statistical adjustment for structural confounders across municipalities, such as municipal fiscal revenue, GDP per capita, utility governance structure (state company vs. municipal department), demographic scale, or physical terrain.

Provides thorough institutional analysis of federal-municipal sanitation governance, including repeated federal decree postponements of the PMSB deadline weakening compliance incentives, STJ tariff jurisprudence allowing collection charges without treatment (incentivizing collection over treatment), and concrete operational barriers in municipal e-SIC portals.

Publicly available secondary sources (SNIS, IBGE MUNIC 2017, SEI 2017, BCB IGP-DI) allow partial replication, but primary 2019 e-SIC and physical protocol responses are not deposited in a public archive and Figures 1-2 lack horizontal-axis municipality labels.

Clearly categorizes all 20 municipalities across mutually exclusive PMSB statuses (Table 2), SNIS completeness and e-SIC organ registration (Quadro 1), and four LAI response outcomes (Table 3), although the exact verbatim text of the LAI information request is not reproduced.

raw_response.overall_narrative_summary: Carvalho, Jesus Júnior, and Gomes (2022) present a doctrinal-empirical legal-institutional study evaluating compliance with Brazil's National Basic Sanitation Policy (Lei 11.445/2007 and Decreto 7.217/2010) and Access to Information Law (Lei 12.527/2011) across all 20 municipalities whose urban headquarters lie in the Eastern Watersheds (Bacias Hidrográficas do Leste, BHL) of Bahia in 2016-2017. Although the abstract describes the study as 'quali-quantitativa', it conducts neither primary qualitative interviewing/thematic analysis nor statistical/quasi-experimental inference; rather, it combines doctrinal legal analysis with descriptive tabulation of SNIS, IBGE MUNIC 2017, and SEI indicators and a primary Freedom of Information (e-SIC and physical LAI) compliance audit of the 13 municipalities lacking complete SNIS data. Under the Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework (structured non-validated judgment), the study is strong in legal source accuracy, jurisdictional specificity, outcome definition, census framing of the 20 watershed seats, and institutional contextualization (highlighting repeated federal PMSB deadline postponements, STJ jurisprudence permitting sewage tariff collection without treatment, and defective municipal e-SIC portals). Methodological limitations include substantial municipal non-reporting and LAI non-response (restricting quantitative service and investment indicators to 12-17 municipalities), minor presentation defects in the published PDF (missing horizontal-axis municipality labels in Figures 1 and 2, a 12-vs-13 municipality count discrepancy in Table 1, and a single slip citing STF instead of STJ on p. 20), absence of researcher reflexivity, and the lack of any causal identification strategy or confounding control to support causal attributions.
raw_response.overall_rating: Adequate descriptive legal-institutional evidence, weak for causal inference (structured non-validated judgment)
raw_response.study_design_identified: Doctrinal-empirical legal-institutional compliance study combining Brazilian sanitation/transparency law analysis with descriptive administrative data (SNIS, IBGE MUNIC 2017) and a primary Freedom of Information (LAI / e-SIC) audit across 20 watershed municipalities (2016-2017)
raw_response.where_found_summary: Study scope, 20-municipality BHL census, and data collection methods (SNIS, IBGE MUNIC 2017, e-SIC/physical LAI requests) are on PDF pp. 3-6 (Abstract and Section 1); doctrinal legal analysis is on PDF pp. 6-17 (Section 2); empirical indicators, maps, and LAI audit tables are on PDF pp. 17-27 (Section 3, Figures 1-4, Tables 1-3, Quadro 1); conclusions are on PDF pp. 28-29 (Section 4).
raw_response.why_tool_chosen: Despite self-describing as 'quali-quantitativa' in the abstract, the study conducts neither qualitative primary research (no interviews, focus groups, or qualitative thematic coding) nor analytical cross-sectional regression or quasi-experimental evaluation. Instead, it is a classic doctrinal-empirical hybrid / jurimetric-administrative compliance case study published in a law journal that pairs doctrinal analysis of Lei 11.445/2007, Decreto 7.217/2010, STJ precedent, and Lei 12.527/2011 with descriptive municipal sanitation indicators and a primary LAI/e-SIC audit across 20 Bahia municipalities, matching the Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework under RISK_OF_BIAS.md §§1-2.
